records.mutation: separate the candidate list per reading (divisors vs all smaller values) and force a check of symmetric/extremal candidates
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 0/8 with 5 of 8 truncating at the token cap; every rollout built only the divisor pairs of the displayed number and then applied that same divisor list to the sum reading, so both readings looked contradictory and the student either looped re-deriving the same two cases or emitted a divisor it had already refuted. The incumbent flags label ambiguity but never says each reading induces a different candidate list, and it never prompts the symmetric or extremal candidate that a divisor enumeration cannot reach, so I added both plus a stricter no-restart rule.

records.mutation: make the spot-check itself robust: evaluate sample points via modulus identities, and on conflict test a second instance rather than re-auditing the derivation
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 5.7k-9.1k tokens; the lone failure reached the correct locus equation quickly, then mis-evaluated one sample point (a dropped reciprocal/sign when inverting the map), and because the incumbent told it to recheck that one line it re-audited the same correct derivation roughly sixty times and burned the full 16384-token cap without ever committing a result. So the incumbent's no-restart rule fires but sends the student into a self-audit loop; I therefore make the check cheap and self-correcting (use modulus identities to evaluate an instance, and on conflict test a different instance instead of re-reading the derivation, since two agreeing instances outweigh one disagreeing one) and move the commit instruction ahead of all checking.

records.mutation: add output-budget discipline: lead the visible reply with the result, ban restating the setup after reasoning closes
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts scored; all eight reached the correct value early (within the first ~9k of ~55-62k characters), so the incumbent's containment and symmetry advice is working and is kept. The decisive new detail is that three of the four failures did close the reasoning block but then spent every remaining token re-introducing the setup, redefining coordinates and re-deriving the union identity, and were truncated before emitting any result; so this revision reallocates tokens from the wedge wording to an explicit short-output rule that puts the result on the first visible line and forbids restating the problem afterwards.

records.mutation: state that pieces are reusable so the piece count is never the cap; disambiguate residual-vanishing from the progression's own step
records.subagent_summary: The incumbent scored only 2 of 8 fresh rollouts (train_i=0.25), well below its 0.625 last round, so the signal is high-variance. The dominant failure, in 4 of the 8, was answering the number of available objects: each rollout insisted every progression term needs its own distinct polynomial, and one further collapsed the summed per-object budget back to a single residual's root count. The revision therefore declares pieces reusable and reserves the word difference for the progression's step, naming the residual separately.

records.mutation: target sign/factor slips in the elimination step with numeric back-substitution and a redo-that-step-only rule, plus shared-vertex cross product for area
records.subagent_summary: Only three of eight fresh rollouts were correct: three died at the 16384-token cap still mid-elimination, one mangled a sign while moving the constant across the logarithm and then declared the system unsolvable before asserting an invented area, and one solved a wrongly cross-multiplied quadratic, took the extraneous root, and then applied the shoelace formula to a self-intersecting vertex order. The incumbent asks for verification by a second method but never says what to verify, so I made the check concrete (numerically substitute each candidate root into the original conditions), localized the retry to the failing elimination step instead of a full restart, and replaced the ambiguous area step with a cross product of two edge vectors from a shared vertex.

records.mutation: replace the first-vs-last hedge with the concrete LIFO orientation fact (a pile's bottom is its earliest arrival) and forbid reading 'bottom' as 'moved last'
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; six rollouts terminated normally at 11k-15k tokens and two hit the cap while relitigating, so length is secondary. Every failure on the second part came from one shared root cause: the rollouts equated the requested bottom slot with 'the item moved last' and then priced that event by an asserted uniform draw (1/n, 1/(n-1)) or by dividing a permutation count by a branch count, while two more collapsed the whole process to certainty. The revision therefore replaces the incumbent's vague 'FIRST or LAST arrival' hedge with the explicit last-in-first-out orientation rule, bans the 'bottom means moved last' reading, and keeps the free-versus-forced 1/2 accounting that transferred best in earlier rounds while naming 1/2^(all moves) as an additional wrong denominator.

records.mutation: add index-vs-exponent representation check and a substitute-once no-re-solve rule
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling scored 2 of 8 and all six failures hit the 16384-token cap. Every one of them died the same way: after solving a tiny case they recast the problem as a polynomial, silently swapped which variable was the summation index and which was the exponent, discovered the mismatch, and then spent thousands of tokens oscillating between the two readings and re-solving the same 3x3 system with different arithmetic each pass. The revision therefore front-loads an explicit index-versus-exponent check on the smallest case before any reinterpretation and replaces open-ended re-derivation with a single substitute-back verification that closes the case.

records.mutation: compress rather than extend: recast the divisibility scaffold in unit-generic wording at incumbent length, naming gcd inline and replacing the vague integrality/units clause with multiply-back plus early bare-number commitment
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 10-16k characters, so train_i stays saturated at 1.0 and every point of gain must come from transfer. Every prior proposal for this hint grew the text (112-138 tokens) and every one lost transfer ground, while the rollouts still spend 20-70 restatements per trace re-litigating per-unit versus whole-collection scope and 13-23 restatements circling the gcd, so this round tests the opposite axis: same 81-token budget as the incumbent, unit-generic nouns so the scaffold applies beyond this setting, gcd named inline, and a decide-once plus multiply-back plus commit-to-a-bare-number close in place of the vague integrality-and-units clause.

records.mutation: immunize the centered family against self-inflicted sign/parity objections and treat a degenerate center as an arithmetic slip to redo in place rather than a cue to abandon the ansatz
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct, all finishing under 13k tokens by adopting the shared-center antisymmetric pair and solving the two given values by sum and difference; the single failure ran to the 16384-token cap after reaching that exact ansatz twice, then discarding it because it mis-added the two given values into a degenerate center and separately convinced itself the inner-plus-outer sign parity forbade odd k, after which it fell back to naming coefficients and expanding the degree-nine composition. The revision therefore pre-refutes the parity objection by noting both compositions reduce to the same form, and reclassifies a degenerate or value-clashing center as a one-line arithmetic slip to repair in place instead of grounds to change methods.

records.mutation: forbid untraced cycle-structure period claims, make refuted periods permanently discarded, and require the closed form to fit the smallest verified count so off-by-one exponents get corrected instead of relitigated
records.subagent_summary: Only 1 of 8 rollouts scored; 6 hit the 16384-token cap and one filled its budget with a literally repeating sentence. The shared mechanism was asserting a period from unverified cycle-structure narration, then re-raising the same refuted candidate dozens of times and settling on an off-by-one exponent that contradicted its own smallest verified case. The revision therefore bans untraced period claims, forces refuted candidates to stay discarded, and makes disagreement with the smallest verified count diagnose an exponent slip in the formula rather than reopen the case.
